$comment: Deliberate exceptions to scripts/sast.mjs. One entry = one file the rule fires on, with the reason it is correct anyway. Reviewed under CODEOWNERS. An exception with no reason string is ignored (i.e. still fails), so 'add it to the list' is never a one-word edit. When the finding disappears the gate reports the entry as stale — delete it.

route-auth.src/app/api/skills/route.ts: Diagnostics surface, not a user surface: it returns the registered AI skill ids and the gate-covered set — build-time facts identical for every caller, with no tenant, no project id and no provider call. Importing the registry is itself the check (registration throws on an incomplete skill), which is the point of being able to curl it.
route-auth.src/app/api/images/upload-ref/route.ts: Deliberately anonymous: the Creative Studio reference upload has to work for a signed-out visitor on the marketing site. It is not unguarded — durableGuard applies both the per-minute AI throttle and a per-IP DAILY cap (RATE_RULES.uploadRefPerDay), and it spends no AI units. Adding an auth requirement is a product decision, not a bug fix.
route-auth.src/app/api/sken/claim/route.ts: Deliberately anonymous: stores a visitor's own sanitized scan under a 128-bit random token so it survives the sign-in redirect. No AI spend, no tenant read; durableGuard per-IP daily cap (RATE_RULES.skenPerDay) + 32 KB body cap.
route-auth.src/app/api/feed/[token]/route.ts: Deliberately anonymous: a merchant feed is pulled by Google/Heureka/Zboží robots that cannot sign in. The 128-bit random token in the path IS the credential (unguessable, per-project, revocable by re-mint); the route is read-only, spends no AI units, and serves only the catalog the owner explicitly exposed.
route-auth.src/app/api/twin/inbound/[token]/route.t: Deliberately anonymous: the callers are machines (a Meta page webhook, a mail forwarder, a Google Business bridge) that cannot sign in. TWO things together are the credential: the 128-bit random token in the path (unguessable, per-(project, channel), revocable by re-mint) and an HMAC over the RAW BODY under that endpoint's own encrypted secret, checked BEFORE the body is parsed. The Adamant flavour is replay-bounded to 5 minutes; Meta's timestamp-less flavour is covered by the intake being idempotent (a replayed body mints the same draft ids). 64 KB cap, no AI spend, no read-back. ADR-0002 holds inverted: (userId, projectId, channel) come out of the stored row the owner-guarded management route wrote, never from the wire — so the only thing a valid request can do is append a pending draft to the token's OWN project.

sql-template-interpolation.src/lib/db.ts: PRAGMA table_info(${table}) — PRAGMA takes no bound parameters, so this cannot be written with a placeholder. `table` is only ever a literal from SCHEMA/MIGRATIONS in this same file; no caller-supplied value reaches it.
sql-template-interpolation.src/lib/leads/store.local.ts: DELETE FROM ${t} — a table NAME cannot be bound. `t` iterates a literal array of three table names written inline in clearProjectLeads(); the project id in the same statement IS bound (WHERE project_id = ?).
sql-template-interpolation.src/lib/projects/orphan-walk.local.ts: SELECT DISTINCT tenant FROM ${quoted(table)} — a table NAME cannot be bound, and unlike the two entries above the name is NOT a literal from this file: the dependent-side orphan walk enumerates the live schema from sqlite_master on purpose, so a per-project table nobody registered is still walked. The value is therefore the database's own catalogue rather than anything a request reaches, and it goes through quoted(), which applies SQLite identifier quoting with "" doubling. The statement is read-only and selects no caller-supplied value.
